question.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3+\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i} \\ 2+4\text{i} \\ 3-4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4-7\text{i} \\ 1-2\text{i} \\ 3+\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-5+\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-3\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$

current_example.problem:
Consider the vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_3$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2 \times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14245038/assets/4d796869c8cc9a220581c8bb229677cc76a9c901f4f5dc6f8570987c0602f6ad.svg)
The vectors $\mathbf{v}_1$ and $\mathbf{v}_3$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues $\lambda_1=7 + 4\textrm{i}$ and $\lambda_3=-3 + 2\textrm{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PBP^{-1},$ find a possible matrix $P.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\qquad$ ${\color{red}\lambda_1}=\overline{\color{red}\lambda}_{\color{red}2} \quad$ and $\quad {\color{blue}\lambda_3}=\overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\qquad$ ${\color{red}\mathbf{v}_1} = \overline{\color{red}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{red}2} \quad$ and $\quad {\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_3} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}4},$ 

then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14245038/assets/171c55873c5110fba1bcf81f206e24558cdd9a63cd983ef5f1ab3a758ddf3d95.svg)
and
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14245038/assets/8351ffa18e3db0dcc4492c623b589569b351161c1f3a2744235a37b8a90419c7.svg)
Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14245038/assets/b64b88d3cb621a66d0318b691d4cb8dfccff50d76bffe8023f11d46754b233dd.svg)
we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${\color{red}{\mathbf{v}_1}},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_3}.$ Therefore,
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14245038/assets/08d48d1ba018eca02106a4d66febfe23cd26d7ecbcc335d18d81d10e4e2fa2a1.svg)
